policy.records: Only the reads that differ from what LibreOffice made of the same file, and only the renders that do not land in the clean band. Everything this suite exercises that is absent from the two lists below is asserted to agree, so a new difference fails by not being listed.
policy.reproduce: A row that stops reproducing fails too. That is deliberate: a fix should arrive with this file updated, so the shrinking of the suspected-defect list is a thing somebody can point at. A render that comes back better than the band recorded here fails for the same reason - an improvement nobody records is an improvement nobody can show.
policy.states: documented - a limitation one of the conformance documents states. suspected-defect - a difference nobody decided on, which is what comparing against another implementation is actually good for. accepted - this component's own behaviour, looked at and accepted.
policy.reviewer: A row is not classified by being written down. documented and accepted both need a reviewer and a date, and a documented row needs a reference to the conformance document that states the limitation, which the guard checks is really there. This is the same demand CorpusControlGuardTests makes of the corpus baseline and PdfTestControlGuardTests makes of the tool manifest.
policy.toolchain: producedWith pins the LibreOffice build, the PDF text extractor, the font set, the platform and the dpi these rows were measured on. A run whose own stamp does not match it does not compare against these rows: it skips, and the skip names the mismatch. LibreOffice's layout moves between releases and with whatever fonts it can find, so a row measured on another machine is a claim about that machine, and quietly reading it as a claim about this one is how a suite comes to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the change under test.
policy.empty: Both lists ship empty and every producedWith field is null, because nothing has been measured here against an approved, pinned toolchain yet. That is the shipped state on purpose, and it is not the same as having no opinion. An empty file says plainly that nothing has been measured; a file generated against whatever LibreOffice happened to be installed that morning looks like evidence, and would be worse than no baseline for exactly that reason. tests/corpus/external-sources.json ships with no rows on the same argument.
policy.bands: A render row records bands, not numbers. The numbers under observed are there for a reader, and for hysteresis when a run sits on a threshold; the verdict is the band. Rasterized comparison numbers move with antialiasing, hinting and the version of the font that got installed, so a file that recorded them as the expectation would fail on a change nobody can see and pass on one anybody could.

reads.why: Not a difference at all - the text projections agree, and the row exists only because the read raised html.css.rule. That is the codec reporting that it skipped a stylesheet rule whose selector it does not implement, which here is the 'td p' and 'th p' that LibreOffice writes for a table. Reporting it is the behaviour this component asks of a codec, so the row records a codec doing the right thing loudly. docs/html-conformance.md states exactly which selector is matched and which are not, and why the line is drawn there.
reads.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the first office baseline

reads.why: Not a difference this component could avoid. LibreOffice's HTML export has no way to write a frame, so it flattens both of the seed's frames to GIF files beside the document and links them; the reader never fetches an external resource and reports html.skip.external once per read, which docs/html-conformance.md states outright in both directions. What the row is worth recording for is what it says about the corpus rather than about the codec: the html target of this seed measures a document with the construct taken out of it, so a reader comparing the four targets knows not to read agreement here as evidence about frames.
reads.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the letterhead and line-break seeds

reads.why: The same defect as the text row for this document, one step further on. The stray 2 the RTF reader lifts out of the footer's PAGE field is written into our ODT export as body text, and LibreOffice reads it back from there. It is the interop check doing what it is for: a reader defect that stops at our model is ours to find, and one that reaches a file somebody else opens is worth a louder row.

reads.why: A page number escapes from the footer into the body. LibreOffice writes the seed's footer as {\footer ... Page {\field{\*\fldinst PAGE}{\fldrslt 2}}}, and broilerdoc's text projection opens with a bare 2 that LibreOffice's does not. The word Page beside it is correctly absent, so the reader is skipping the footer destination's own text and keeping the text inside \fldrslt - a field result is body text only when the field is in the body. It also puts the number in the wrong place twice over: the render for this document draws the footer as Page with nothing after it.

reads.why: A limitation docs/html-conformance.md states outright: the HTML writer does not emit list structure and reports html.list when it drops it, so a list read from HTML does not survive a round trip back through HTML. The roadmap holds HTML list writing as deliberate and unimplemented, to be reconsidered only behind conformance fixtures and explicit diagnostics. The diagnostic is the codec saying what it dropped, which is the half that makes the limitation reviewable.

renders.why: Three defects on one document, and the ink box is measuring the third. The bordered box anchored in the body is not drawn on page one: it and the header's band are both foreground shapes, DocumentLayout appends running-content shapes after the body's, and the rasterizer draws every foreground shape in list order - so the band is painted last and over the box. Both files state the stacking and neither is read: draw:z-index 0 and 1 in the ODF, relativeHeight 2 and 3 in the DOCX, and DocumentShape says as much in its own summary. The box then appears on page two, where the document anchors it to a paragraph on page one. And the 1154 px is a footer drawn on page one where LibreOffice draws none - w:titlePg is set and the section declares no first-page footer, and the flag is not read - carrying the PAGE field's stale cached result, 0 in the source and 2 here.

The frames are gone from this target before broilerdoc sees it. LibreOffice's HTML export writes them as GIF files beside the document, the reader never fetches an external resource, and the text row for the same document carries the html.skip.external that says so. So the band and the box are absent on our side and drawn on LibreOffice's, and the 0.48 profile is measuring that rather than anything about the HTML codec. The row is kept rather than the target dropped, because a target quietly missing from the corpus is worse than one whose weakness is written down.
renders.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the letterhead and line-break seeds

renders.why: Three defects, two of them ODT's own. The band's gradient runs left to right instead of top to bottom: LibreOffice 24.2 writes draw:angle="30deg" and OdtReader parses the attribute as a bare number of tenths of a degree, so TryParse fails on the unit and the false branch yields zero - and a failed parse reaches the same branch as an absent attribute, so nothing is reported. A unit-aware parse alone would not settle it either: LibreOffice's own DOCX export of this shape writes ang="3600000", sixty degrees, where the ODF says thirty, and the DOCX path draws it correctly. The band is also repeated on page two and the page number never appears at all, because the reader resolves the master page the body starts on - correctly, through style:master-page-name - files its header into the Default slot, and never follows style:next-style-name to the Continuation master or reads its footer. The bordered box is hidden under the band as in the docx row, for the reason that row gives.

The tightest ink box of the four at 31 px, and a poor profile for reasons the box cannot see. LibreOffice writes both shapes into the body here rather than into a header destination, so the stacking accident the docx and odt rows describe does not happen and the bordered box is the one place in this corpus where it is visible - but both shapes are then repeated on page two, where the document puts neither. The gradient runs left to right, as it does through ODT. And the stray 2 the text row for this document records is drawn at the head of the body while the footer reads Page with nothing after it.

A forced line break is not a break in layout. Every codec reads text:line-break, w:br, \line and
as U+2028, which is the model's own line-break character - RichTextEditor.InsertLineBreak inserts exactly that - and DocumentLayout then classifies characters with char.IsWhiteSpace, for which U+2028 is true. So the break arrives as an ordinary break opportunity, the seed's five-line address reflows onto two wrapped lines, and everything after it moves up the page. The tokenizer has no mandatory-break fragment to fall into: it distinguishes whitespace, tab and image and nothing else. Four targets failing at the same profile similarity is the signature of a layout defect rather than a codec one, and the semantic axis is silent by construction - the text canonicalisation maps U+2028 to a newline on both sides before comparing, so no comparison of text can tell an honoured break from a lost one.

Recorded from the first run on the pinned toolchain as the state of the two engines on this date, so a later run that moves is a change somebody can point at rather than a number nobody had.
renders.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the first office baseline
